postings.title: Counsel, Government Contracts & Public Sector
postings.description:
About Virtru:

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We're setting data free so that you can intentionally share it with others, but without sacrificing security, privacy, or control.

We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. Through the Trusted Data Format (TDF) open standard, we're not just protecting data; we're creating a new paradigm where security enables sharing rather than preventing it.

Think of us as the Android of data protection: a robust platform with an open core that developers and partners can build upon, coupled with our own best-in-class applications that showcase what's possible when you reimagine security from the ground up.

Backed by Iconiq Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundry Capital, and Tiger Global, we're helping Fortune 500 companies and government agencies discover that true data security means having the freedom to share, collaborate, and innovate — without compromise.
Compensation: $150,000-165,000/year

Team & Position Details:

As Counsel supporting Government Contracts & Public Sector, you will be reporting to the SVP & General Counsel. We are seeking a lawyer with substantial government contracts experience to help grow our public sector business. You will work directly with the General Counsel and partner with our public sector, sales, finance, security, product, and engineering teams. The role offers meaningful responsibility for negotiations, practical compliance advice, and decisions affecting how a technology company serves government customers. You will lead day-to-day legal support for U.S. public sector contracting, with particular emphasis on federal subcontracts, software licensing, and relationships with prime contractors, systems integrators, resellers, and other partners. You will help colleagues understand which government requirements apply to Virtru, negotiate appropriate commitments, and translate those commitments into workable business practices. This is a hands-on individual contributor position. We value careful legal analysis, strong drafting, sound judgment, and the ability to resolve issues independently while recognizing when to escalate them.

As Counsel, your responsibilities will include:

- Draft, review, and negotiate government subcontracts, software and SaaS agreements, teaming agreements, nondisclosure agreements, reseller and distribution agreements, and related public sector transactions.

- Analyze FAR, DFARS, and agency-specific provisions, including the applicability and scope of proposed flow-down requirements to commercial software and services.

- Support proposals and solicitations by reviewing legal terms, representations and certifications, eligibility requirements, and contractual risks. Partner with business and finance teams on pricing-related legal requirements.

- Advise on contract administration, modifications, renewals, performance issues, disputes, and termination rights.

- Work with security and compliance colleagues on contractual and regulatory requirements involving controlled unclassified information, cybersecurity, incident reporting, CMMC, and applicable NIST standards.

- Advise on procurement integrity, organizational conflicts of interest, gifts and business courtesies, former government personnel restrictions, and other government contracting ethics requirements.

- Identify and advise on export control and sanctions issues, including ITAR and EAR requirements, coordinating with specialist counsel when appropriate.

- Support responses to customer inquiries, audits, investigations, and potential compliance concerns, working with the General Counsel and relevant internal teams.

- Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments and explain their practical consequences for Virtru’s contracts, products, and business operations.

- Develop contract templates, negotiation guidance, training, and practical compliance resources that help colleagues handle recurring issues consistently.

- Support state and local government and education transactions, and other commercial legal matters, as business needs require.

Skills that will help you thrive in this role:

- Juris Doctor from an accredited law school.

- Active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar or the District of Columbia, and the ability to satisfy any applicable in-house counsel registration or other practice requirements where you work.

- At least five years of relevant legal experience advising on U.S. government contracts, gained in a law firm, government agency, corporate legal department, or a combination of these settings.

- Substantial experience drafting and negotiating federal contracts or subcontracts, including experience advising technology companies or negotiating software, SaaS, cloud, or related technology transactions.

- Strong working knowledge of the FAR and DFARS, including commercial product and service contracting, subcontract flow-downs, and government rights in software and technical data.

- Experience advising on government contracting compliance and translating legal requirements into clear recommendations and operational guidance.

- Strong drafting, negotiation, analytical, and communication skills.

- Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise independent judgment, and work effectively with colleagues across legal, technical, and business functions.

Preferred Experience:

- Advising a software, cybersecurity, cloud, or other technology business serving federal customers.

- Negotiating with federal prime contractors, systems integrators, and public sector channel partners.

- Working with defense or intelligence community customers.

- Advising on CUI, CMMC, federal cybersecurity requirements, export controls, or classified-contract requirements.

- Supporting state and local government or education contracting.

- Developing legal templates, training, or compliance processes for a growing business.

Virtruvian qualities that will set you up for success:

- Thinking outside of the box to respectfully challenge your teammates and managers in the pursuit of excellence

- Strong sense of urgency with an action-oriented mindset

- Able to collaborate and adapt to shifting priorities as business needs evolve

- Comfortable with asynchronous communication including slack, email, zoom, etc.

Perks & Benefits:

At Virtru, we believe people do their best work when their wellbeing is put first. This is why we make your wellbeing our priority with a thoughtful and holistic program that encompasses Occupational, Mental, Social, Physical, and Environmental Wellness by offering benefits such as…

- A Flexible PTO policy — we strongly encourage you to take time off (in addition to 14 holidays) to ensure that you are getting the proper time needed to unplug and recharge.

- A $1,500 annual Learning & Development Stipend focused on providing you the resources to continually learn and professionally grow.

- Frequent company-sponsored team celebrations that provide ample opportunities to connect with teammates and be social!

- Access to an Employee Assistance Program

- Access to Headspace, a mental health app tailored to your specific needs.

- A flat 3% contribution to your retirement account

- A high degree of flexibility — Have an appointment, errand, or family emergency to take care of? Hop to it! We give you the time and space to take care of you and your own first.

In addition to wellbeing, Virtru places a strong emphasis on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Our DB&I Council is dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace and making the psychological safety of each and every one of our teammates a top priority. 

Additional perks include: 

- Competitive compensation

- Generous parental, medical, and bereavement policies

- Uncapped commissions for Sales roles

- 401K contribution and stock options

- Full medical, dental, and vision benefits

- New Hire Swag and IT Welcome boxes

- Structured semi-annual 360° performance reviews

postings.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Security Clearance Required
postings.description:
About Virtru:

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We're setting data free so that you can intentionally share it with others, but without sacrificing security, privacy, or control.

We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. Through the Trusted Data Format (TDF) open standard, we're not just protecting data; we're creating a new paradigm where security enables sharing rather than preventing it.

Think of us as the Android of data protection: a robust platform with an open core that developers and partners can build upon, coupled with our own best-in-class applications that showcase what's possible when you reimagine security from the ground up.

Backed by Iconiq Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundry Capital, and Tiger Global, we're helping Fortune 500 companies and government agencies discover that true data security means having the freedom to share, collaborate, and innovate — without compromise.
Compensation: $200,000-225,000/year

Team & Position Details:

Virtru protects data wherever it travels, for customers ranging from commercial enterprises to the Department of Defense, the Intelligence Community, Law Enforcement, and Federal Civilian agencies. Many of these customers run Virtru inside classified mission environments across the Washington, DC region, where the work happens on site next to the customer's own engineers, and where what we ship has to fit systems few people outside the building can see.

As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer in the Delivery Engineering organization, you'd be helping to build a founder team focused on making these deployments simple, easy, and fast. You'll be the senior engineer who can change the software in the room. You'll design and build the integrations, policy enforcement points (the components that enforce access policy inside a customer's application), and deployment tooling our customers need and cannot get from the product alone, and you'll own the technical outcome of each deployment from zero to one and on into production. You'll be embedded with one cleared mission customer and own that account's technical outcome end to end. This location requires a full-scope polygraph

You will work with deployment engineers who run installs and upgrades through our published paths, with solutions architects who shaped each engagement, with QA to prove what you build before it ships, and with our product engineering and Platform Engineering counterparts, who need what you learn in the field as designs and decisions they can act on. You'll also help set the bar for the forward deployed engineers who join after you.

The impact of this role is company and product wide, heavily enabling our goals to scale Virtru, partner, and customer led deployments non-linearly without having to throw more humans at the problem. You'll be expected to come up with AI-native design patterns that will increase our velocity without compromising our high bar for quality and security. The right candidate is excited about working on a small, nimble, highly autonomous and empowered team where everyone is expected to make high judgement, high velocity decisions independently and with urgency. If you want a role where the connection between what you build and what the customer achieves requires no explaining, this is one.

As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, your responsibilities will include:

- Design and ship software inside cleared customer environments. Integrations, policy enforcement points, connectors, and deployment tooling, written in Go, Python, Java, or Rust, reviewed, tested with QA, and built so the next customer can reuse them.

- Own the technical outcome of each deployment you're staffed to. From the first environment review through production and upgrade, you are the engineer accountable for the platform working in the customer's systems, across Kubernetes, Windows estates, identity providers, and air-gapped classified networks.

- Turn field lessons into product decisions. Write designs and architecture decision records that weigh a product fix against a field workaround, take them to our product engineering teams with evidence, and see them through to a decision.

- Resolve conflicts between a customer's accreditation boundary and the platform's requirements by changing the design, and write the pattern down so the next engagement inherits it.

- Diagnose failures down to source code, whether the cause sits in our software, in the customer's environment, or in the space between them.

- Build validated configurations for identity providers beyond our reference setup, such as PingFederate, Entra ID, and Okta, so the next customer configures what you built instead of starting over.

- Work inside codebases other teams own, and leave them better tested and documented than you found them.

- Package what you build so it installs, upgrades, and runs in disconnected environments under STIG hardening and FIPS constraints.

- Partner with deployment engineers so standard installs follow the published path, and hand them what you build with documentation, test evidence, and a clear way to report back.

- Explain your designs to customer security reviewers and accrediting officials, and answer their follow-up questions.

- Mentor other forward deployed engineers, review their code and designs, and help define how we interview and level for the role.

- Use AI coding agents as part of your daily workflow, and help the team learn which patterns raise quality and speed together.

- This role requires residence in the DMV and on-site work at customer locations at least 50% of the time, and may require travel to other customer sites in the DC region.

Skills that will help you thrive in this role:

- Must haves

- An active TS/SCI US security clearance. The Fort Meade location also requires a full-scope polygraph. This role will work in classified environments at least 50% of the time.

- You ship production code today, and other people reuse what you design. You write and review code in Go, Python, Java, or Rust as part of your current job, and you can walk us through a component you designed that another team or customer adopted.

- You have made software work in environments you did not build. You have diagnosed identity, certificate, or Kubernetes failures in a classified, accredited, or customer production environment from logs, without the original author on the call, and changed a design to fit the environment rather than asking for an exception.

- Nice to haves

- Kubernetes across more than one distribution, such as OpenShift, Rancher, or RKE2, including Helm packaging.

- Delivering software into air-gapped environments: offline registries, bundle transfer, and upgrades with no network.

- Identity and authorization integration: OIDC, SAML, PingFederate, Entra ID, Okta, CAC or PIV, and attribute-based access control (ABAC).

- Windows and .NET depth: Windows Services, signed installers, Active Directory, and Group Policy.

- DISA STIGs, FIPS 140, and the Risk Management Framework from the delivery side.

- Familiarity with Zero Trust security architecture and concepts such as Policy Enforcement and Decision Points, cryptography, and identity.

- Design documents or decision records another team adopted.

- Experience building with AI coding agents.

- Prior forward deployed, embedded, or customer-site engineering work with Intelligence Community or Department of Defense customers.

- Where this role may not be a fit

- Having stepped away from writing code. If your recent work is advising, configuring, or reviewing rather than writing and shipping code yourself, this role may not be for you.

- Wanting a product-only role with no customer contact. Much of this job is working next to customers, in their environments, on their problems. If you prefer to build away from customers, this role may not be for you.

- Inability to earn trust and credibility with partners and customers. You may be the person who has to explain to a skeptical government security team why our software is safe, or to an internal VP of Engineering why we need to prioritize critical platform features. Those have to be conversations you are willing and excited to have.

Virtruvian qualities that will set you up for success:

- Thinking outside of the box to respectfully challenge your teammates and managers in the pursuit of excellence

- Strong sense of urgency with an action-oriented mindset

- Able to collaborate and adapt to shifting priorities as business needs evolve

- Comfortable with asynchronous communication including slack, email, zoom, etc.

Perks & Benefits:

At Virtru, we believe people do their best work when their wellbeing is put first. This is why we make your wellbeing our priority with a thoughtful and holistic program that encompasses Occupational, Mental, Social, Physical, and Environmental Wellness by offering benefits such as…

- A Flexible PTO policy — we strongly encourage you to take time off (in addition to 14 holidays) to ensure that you are getting the proper time needed to unplug and recharge.

- A $1,500 annual Learning & Development Stipend focused on providing you the resources to continually learn and professionally grow.

- Access to an Employee Assistance Program

In addition to wellbeing, Virtru places a strong emphasis on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Our DB&I Council is dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace and making the psychological safety of each and every one of our teammates a top priority.

The impact of this role is company and product wide, heavily enabling our goals to scale Virtru, partner, and customer led deployments non-linearly without having to throw more humans at the problem. You'll be expected to come up with AI-native design patterns that will increase our velocity without compromising our high bar for quality and security. The right candidate is excited about working on a small, nimble, highly autonomous and empowered team where everyone is expected to make high judgement, high velocity decisions independently and with urgency. If you want a role where the connection between what you build and what the customer achieves requires no explaining, this is one.

As a Senior Software Engineer in Delivery Engineering, your responsibilities will include:

- Build custom integrations and policy enforcement points for cleared customers, scoped against a statement of work, tested with QA, and delivered into environments Virtru does not operate.

- Work directly with customer engineers inside cleared environments to understand their systems, agree what will be built, and explain your design to their security team.

- Turn what you build twice into a reusable asset. When a second customer needs the same thing, the first build becomes a template, a library, or a tool that deployment engineers and forward deployed engineers can use without you.

- Build on the SDKs and APIs that our product engineering teams maintain, and bring gaps and defects back to them with a clear reproduction and a documented outcome.

- Write code that follows the engineering standard set by Delivery Engineering's Principal Software Engineer, and submit your work to the design review that standard calls for.

- Package your work so it installs, upgrades, and runs in disconnected environments with no path to the internet.

- Partner with deployment engineers and forward deployed engineers so the person who installs your work in the field has what they need: documentation, test evidence, and a clear way to report back.

- Partner with our Platform Engineering counterparts on how your work is built, signed, and released.

- Use AI coding agents as part of your daily workflow, and help the team learn which patterns raise quality and speed together.

- Mentor and learn from peers across the organization, and help define what good looks like for customer-facing engineering at Virtru.

- This role may require travel up to 25% of the time.

- Must haves

- An active TS/SCI US security clearance. This role will work in classified environments at least 25% of the time.

- You have built and shipped production software. You have owned code from design through release and maintenance, in a language and stack you can discuss in depth, and you can show us what you built and what you would do differently.

- You can explain a design to a skeptical government security team. You can take a customer's security reviewers through what your software does, what it touches, and why it is safe to run, and you can answer the follow-up questions.

- Nice to haves

- Windows and .NET depth: production .NET on Windows, including Windows Services, signed installers, and managed distribution. Many of our customers' end-user environments are Windows-heavy, and some of our policy enforcement points deploy on Windows client endpoints.

- Go proficiency, which is what the Data Security Platform and OpenTDF are written in.

- Kubernetes experience, including packaging and running software across more than one distribution.

- Identity and authorization integration experience: OIDC, SAML, and attribute-based access control (ABAC).

- Establish the infrastructure-as-code baseline for a standard deployment, so every deployment and upgrade starts from a known state.

- Instrument deployments so we can measure time to value, upgrade lag, first-time-right rate, and cost per deployment, and hand that telemetry to our Operations partners to support continuous improvement.

- Design for disconnected operation from the start. In classified and air-gapped environments automated telemetry may be difficult or prohibitive to collect, so every collector needs a mode where a human reviews a local file and releases it.

- Carry field findings into product decisions with a documented outcome, so the same class of deployment failure does not arrive a second time.
